correctness.rationale: Enumerating quadratic residues Q={1,3,4,9,10,12} yields the unique graph P13. All 8192 subsets are classified by the actual predicates sigma⊆N(v) for some v (neighborhood) and N[v] not subset sigma for all v (dominance); face totals 598 and 7592 and claimed f-vectors follow. Independent reimplementation of deterministic 0..12 vertex-toggle matching gave 286 and 3783 disjoint pairs and critical cells exactly (one 0-cell,25 2-cells) and (one 0-cell,25 8-cells). Independent explicit oriented Hasse adjacency digraphs were completely topologically sorted on all 598 and 7592 faces, establishing acyclicity rather than just Morse counts. Forman’s theorem then yields a CW model with one vertex and only 25 cells of one dimension >=2, i.e. the claimed integral sphere wedges. Multiplication by 2 gives P13 ≅ complement graph; Matsushita–Wakatsuki Alexander duality explains pairing, not individual wedge ranks. The complete finite calculation does not claim all Paley orders.

evidence: Shukla applies to maximum degree <=3 and four-regular circulants; P13 has degree 6.
A Paley17 Moore-space result is fixed order 17, not a stronger family theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither known family hypothesis contains this P13 object; a general Alexander duality theorem does not imply its exact sphere multiplicities.

value.rationale: A motivated exact integral homotopy classification for a canonical strongly regular self-complementary graph central to neighborhood-complex coloring topology and its Alexander-dual domination invariant. Complete finite matchings establish much more than field Betti numbers, without pretending to solve an arbitrary Paley family.

final_claim: For the quadratic-residue Paley graph P13 on F_13, N(P13) ≃ wedge^25 S^2 and its dominance complex D(P13) ≃ wedge^25 S^8 integrally; the two are Alexander-dual graph complexes, with the duality known previously.
limitations: Applies only to P13; no infinite Paley theorem.
An exhaustive single-graph computation can be scientifically valuable, but an unindexed exact table remains a priority risk.
